engagement_background.objective: Advantia Health engaged Treya Partners to identify and capture cost-savings across its spend base (~$45M) by running strategic sourcing events, leveraging GPO contracts, and establishing stronger procurement processes in order to boost EBITDA and enterprise value for its private-equity owners.
engagement_background.scope_summary: Treya will execute savings-creation work in 10 spend categories representing about $19M in addressable spend (e.g., Employee Benefits, Medical Devices, Diagnostic Services, Billing/RCM, Medical Supplies, Telecom, Data Center, Office Supplies).  Activities include competitive RFPs, incumbent negotiations, and a procurement process / controls review; some categories (e.g., Benefits) are optional and Electronic Payment Processing scope is still TBD.
constraints_challenges: Company lacks dedicated strategic procurement resources and has historically focused on day-to-day clinical operations rather than sourcing initiatives.
Spend and item-level usage data are incomplete and spread across two AP / P-card systems (Advantia Mid-Atlantic and Heartland), limiting baseline accuracy.
Supplier base is fragmented due to multiple acquisitions that have not been fully integrated, creating duplication and inconsistent pricing.
Line-item data must often be requested directly from suppliers, some of whom are slow or unwilling to provide information, delaying timelines.
Certain savings opportunities (e.g., IUD discounts) require changing clinic purchasing behaviors or minimum-order practices, which may face end-user resistance.
Aggressive project timeline of roughly 4–6 months (plus a later Benefits wave) adds pressure to collect data, run events, and implement contracts quickly.

procurement_environment.data_availability: AP and corporate card spend extracts (Oct-2020–Sep-2021) are available; contracts and detailed usage reports must be gathered from clinics and suppliers; no centralized contract repository exists.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Multiple systems and vendor naming conventions; limited line-item detail for many suppliers; gaps expected where high-spend suppliers do not provide usage files.
